thread.title: Apple - It's Not About 'Value For Money' Anymore - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)

author: Dilantha De Silva
title: Apple - It's Not About 'Value For Money' Anymore - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)

organizations.name: neutral bank of america merrill lynch

text:
Overview Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ) dropped a bombshell during their Q4 earnings conference call by confirming the management decision to discontinue providing unit sales figures for iPhone, iPad and Mac segments. Unit sales figures provide a meaningful insight into the business model of Apple, and is a major data point scrutinized by analysts to derive year-on-year growth rates. The move received due criticism in early November, and many analysts even downgraded their ratings for Apple soon after, citing concerns over declining iPhone sales volume.

Not only analysts and portfolio managers, the investing public has also voiced their concerns over this move, which is purportedly a move taken to hide a future drop in iPhone unit sales.
This dubious outlook on the future profitability of Apple, combined with the broad market negativity has led the stock price decline of more than 25% since the beginning of November.
Share price movement since November 1
(Source – Morningstar )
To assess whether Apple deserved this beating, implications of not reporting iPhone sales volume should be analyzed.
Why is iPhone unit sales volume so important? Since its launch in 2007, the Apple iPhone has been the driving force of revenues for Apple. During the period of last 6 years, iPhone sales have contributed more than 50% to the company top line, on a consistent basis.
(Source – Statista)
Evidently, Apple’s success as a company depends significantly on revenue generated from its flagship iPhone models. Therefore, analysts are inclined to obtain as much information as possible about iPhone sales to use as inputs to calculate the intrinsic value of the company. In a nutshell, a declining growth rate of iPhone sales volume will be seen as a warning sign, whereas growing iPhone unit sales will be seen as a major value driver.
Over the past half a decade period, it has become a standard practice to forecast iPhone unit sales volume as the starting point of revenue projection. Understandably, top line growth projections were primarily derived by forecasting iPhone unit sales.
In line with this, two conclusions can be drawn regarding the importance of iPhone unit sales volume.
Unit sales volume is important to the company as it is the largest contributor to company revenues and profits. Unit sales volume is important for analysts to determine the intrinsic value of the company, using existing valuation practices. Analysis of the “controversial” decision Market participants, at times, look only at the headline and more often miss the fine print. As a starting point to my analysis, I looked at the guidance provided by the management as to why the decision to discontinue this all important sales figure was taken.
Below is how Apple broke the news.
- Luca Maestri, Chief Financial Officer
In essence, the management views unit sales will eventually become an unimportant consideration in determining company value.
Unit sales growth from 2006-2018
(Source – Statista )
While growth in unit sales figures look impressive over the considered time period, growth has flattened over the last 3 years.
(Source - Author prepared based on company filings)
It is evident how iPad and Mac unit sales have remained flat since 2015, and iPhone unit sales have declined during the same period.
During the same period though, revenues reached all-time highs and the company’s profitability surged to record highs.
(Source - Author prepared based on company filings)
Investors might have been oblivious to this fact, though, that Apple was growing not because of sales volume growth of its mainline products, but because of better pricing and other revenue sources.

The above table is exemplary of how Apple has grown over the last 3 years, despite setbacks in unit sales across its major products.
For sure, deciding not to provide unit sales information is a setback for analysts who are always on the lookout to obtain maximum information about a company, to form a well-informed investment thesis. However, from the company’s perspective, I believe this does little change to its existing structure, the business model or how the company has been beating analyst estimates over the last 3 years.
The Average Selling Price (ASP) of an iPhone is at a historical high, close to $800. This helps explain how Apple has been able to negate effects of declining unit sales by pricing the iPhone better.
(Source – Statista)
At the same time, we need to look at empirical evidence to gauge a measure of Apple’s strength to weather a decline in unit sales.
(Source – Statista)
During the 2015-2016 period, iPhone unit sales declined sharply, triggering a massive decline in revenue. Apple is seeing a surge in revenue, despite flattening unit sales at the moment. This provides evidence of a monumental shift in the business model of Apple, which warrants the company to focus less on unit sales and more on revenue as a standalone figure.
Another important metric to note is that Apple has never really aspired to gain a larger chunk of market share and become the leader by market share. A unit driven approach was not Apple’s strategy, even though Apple continued to report unit sales figures to be as transparent as possible about their business operations and core strategy.
Global smartphone market share by vendor
(Source – IDC )
Global smartphone profit share
(Source – Gadget Match )
Even though Apple has never attempted to become the market leader on a market share basis, Apple has always been able to capture the biggest chunk in global smartphone profits. This clearly speaks of Apple’s strategy and the high margins the company enjoys.
Two conclusions can be drawn from this part of the analysis.
Analysts will certainly be hurt by the decision taken by Apple as they will be forced to project revenue based on an increasing number of assumptions, given the less availability of data. As a result, intrinsic valued derived by analysts will show a greater dispersion. Apple has experienced unit sales declines during the last 3 years. This was identified and addressed by the company management. The company management has identified pricing as one of the strategies to overcome this obstacle. Is price driven growth sustainable for Apple? Top line growth driven by price increases are less adored than volume driven growth, rightly so, as investors want companies to grow organically and sustainably. However, I believe investors should understand the dynamics behind price hikes to ascertain whether such hikes will only inflate revenue in the short term while capping future growth or whether such price hikes have the ability to boost company revenues and profits for an extended period of time.
Pricing strategies are not for every company. Certain companies stand to gain with the use of pricing strategies while other companies tend to lose their market share significantly when their products are marked higher.
The success of using a pricing strategy to drive profits depends on a number of factors, including the below.
Brand value Competition in the industry Availability of substitutes Price elasticity of the product Apple is one of the most sought-after companies in the world and constantly is ranked among companies with the highest brand values.
Not surprisingly, Apple is the company name with the highest brand value, as per latest data from Forbes.
(Source – Forbes )
While Apple enjoys this brand value, competition from its industry rivals has been increasing ever since. Therefore, Apple was never able to properly use its brand power to charge a premium price for its products without taking the risk of losing a significant portion of its revenue due to unit sales declines.
However, in my opinion, the introduction of superior products than its peers will allow Apple to use its brand power to mark their products at a higher price but enjoy stable demand for such products. While competition for Apple products is high at present, Apple is slowly targeting a niche customer base and might probably target the wealthy community in developing markets. Such a segmented approach will put Apple in a superior position and the company will attract little competition from its peers as most of its peer companies are focused on catering to the broader market.
Apple’s brand power is clearly strong enough to allow the company to formulate a growth strategy based on pricing power and competition might diminish if Apple continues to target the upscale market.
Over the last year, the much criticized iPhone X became one of Apple’s most successful products, despite the hefty price tag of $999. Demand for iPhones dropped slightly on a year-over-year basis, which helped Apple report record earnings on the back of higher average selling prices. The price elasticity of Apple products at the higher end of the price spectrum seems to be low, which will benefit Apple in the long run, as the company would be able to gradually increase the price of its high-end products.
Apple’s success based on this model will depend on the company’s ability to develop products and services, which would be adored by users of high-end Apple products.
Apple is now successfully moving away from the generally accepted volume based core-strategy. Notably, the company is changing the “value for money” concept in the smartphone industry. While its peers are focused on providing value for money, Apple is focused on developing best of the breed products, which would be priced much higher than that of its peers.
On the other hand, the company management has time and time again stressed the importance of the services segment.
The services segment has grown at a stellar rate during the last two years and the management expects the services segment revenue to double by 2020.
(Source – Statista)
As the services segment is heavily reliant on the number of Apple devices used on a worldwide basis, there are arguments against the growth projections of the company management as sales volumes are expected to decline. However, one should not forget the fact that existing Apple device users are also eligible to enjoy services provided by Apple, including Apple Pay, Apple Care, Music, and iCloud storage.
The rapid growth of the services segment not only contributes to the overall growth story of Apple but also allows the company to charge a higher price for their flagship devices in the future. Apple might consider selling devices as a packaged bundle, packed with subscriptions to the services they offer.
The competitive position of Apple and its recent shift to target high-end customers, along with the expected growth of the services segment, allows Apple to mark their products higher and grow as a company, even if unit sales decline.
Conclusion Apple is changing dynamically as a company and is no longer dependent on unit sales growth, unlike a few years back. Investors and analysts need to reconsider how they value Apple and embrace the fact that the company need not depend on growing its unit sales to grow as a company. The growing services segment, rising income levels and Apple’s strategy of targeting a niche customer base should all be added up in valuing the company.
Throughout the last couple of months, investors have been keen to beat down Apple shares, as and when a reputed analyst downgraded the stock. However, the consensus estimate still remains above $225. If we leave a margin of safety for intrinsic value calculations and consider $200 as the consensus target price, we are still looking at a return of 21%.
(Source – Tip Ranks )
While it would have been better to have access to sales volume data, the unavailability of such data does not mean the company is set to perform badly in the future. In my opinion, investors should focus on identifying whether strategies adopted by Apple will lead to long-term revenue growth or not, regardless of whether such growth comes from volume gains or price hikes. Apple, as a company, has focused so much on increasing the user experience, for which they would be able to charge a premium price. Finally, Apple is moving on to a position from which they can utilize their brand power as well. More importantly, Apple has lost more than 25% of its share market value since the beginning of November, which provides an additional layer of safety to investors.
Disclosure: I am/we are long AAPL. I wrote this article myself, and it expresses my own opinions. I am not receiving compensation for it (other than from Seeking Alpha). I have no business relationship with any company whose stock is mentioned in this article.
